title: The big rebalance
notes: Charts: rising artists get a bigger lift, radio tours and promotion push your single up that week's chart, and a #1 cools off after a few weeks. A great song from a mid-level star can now reach #1.
Money matters again: quarterly taxes, star overhead (crew, security, glam) and endorsement fees that make sense. A money card shows where it goes.
An 📥 inbox: smaller moments wait for you instead of piling up as pop-ups. In Settings, choose Quiet weeks, Normal or Drama overload.
After every show, see why it went the way it did: skills, band, rehearsal, voice, setlist, production and more.
One clear goal each week with a progress bar, and a career-at-a-glance card on Today.
Real country music: plucked acoustic guitar, bass, brushes, pedal steel and fiddle, with each song playing in its own key and tempo. Sad songs sound sad. Lyrics light up as they play.

Deeper stories: ten-step personal arcs with Juliette, Deacon, Scarlett, Gunnar, Will and Rayna; choices that come back months later; real conversations; your history with every person; and endings based on how you lived.
Career depth: the chart race with your single's journey, album sequencing with a cohesion score, and three kinds of fans (traditional, pop and critics).
Walk Lower Broadway in 3D at night, and characters now blink, talk and turn to face each other.
Move your save to another device with a save code (Settings).
